articles.title: Après PHP, une autre brique essentielle du web doit être mise à jour d'urgence
articles.summary:
C’est la panique sur Internet depuis ce 21 octobre 2026. La raison : deux failles critiques ont été repérées dans le langage informatique PHP, utilisé par des centaines de millions de sites web à travers le monde. La situation se révèle être un vrai casse-tête pour l’Internet mondial, étant donné qu’il est souvent difficile de repérer le langage PHP, omniprésent, mais souvent invisible. En attendant les correctifs, certains sites ont tout simplement décidé de suspendre leur accès, craignant des cyberattaques. C’est notamment le cas d’Orange qui, après avoir connu une panne majeure, a annoncé la suspension temporaire de certains de ses sites et applications par mesure de sécurité. Et la situation ne semble pas vraiment s’arranger pour l’Internet mondial, étant donné que le projet Node.js vient de publier en urgence une série de correctifs de sécurité.
Node.js corrige 10 failles de sécurité, dont quatre critiques
Node.js est un environnement d’exécution qui permet de faire fonctionner du JavaScript en dehors d’un navigateur web, notamment sur des serveurs. Node.js est bien moins répandu que le langage PHP, mais il occupe tout de même une certaine place dans l’Internet mondial. Selon les données de W3Techs du 9 septembre 2026, Node.js est utilisé comme serveur web par 7 % des sites dont le serveur est identifié. Cette proportion atteint toutefois 22 % parmi les 1 000 sites les plus fréquentés. Les risques de perturbation du web mondial sont donc réels en cas de cyberattaque.

articles.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
articles.summary:
Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
Today, Cloudflare is launching a post-quantum geographically restricted key manager in support of our Data Localization Suite (DLS) in closed beta. This new PQ GeoKey Manager is a cornerstone of Cloudflare’s data sovereignty solutions, making sure that a customer's decryption keys are only accessible in their chosen geography. GeoKey Manager implements this by wrapping each decryption key such that it can only be decrypted by Cloudflare servers that are located in the allowed geography.
While general availability (GA) is planned for Q1 2027, today’s launch is an important milestone on our journey to support our customers’ data sovereignty goals while also migrating all Cloudflare products to post-quantum (PQ) cryptography.
Governments, financial institutions, healthcare providers, and defense organizations process highly sensitive data that can remain sensitive for years or decades after it is produced. Encryption is often required to protect this data. When classical, public-key encryption is used, adversaries do not immediately need a quantum computer today to put that data at risk: they can store the ciphertext and retain them until quantum computers can break the public key cryptography protecting it — an attack strategy known as harvest now, decrypt later.

articles.title: Deux jours après PHP2Shell, PHP alerte sur une nouvelle faille qu'il juge « improbable » — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Vous avez mis à jour vos serveurs PHP mercredi ? Le projet a lancé une nouvelle alerte ce vendredi 23 octobre. Dans un court avis « informatif » publié sur php.net, l’équipe de sécurité de PHP décrit une autre faille d’exécution de code à distance, CVE-2026-115560, qui permettrait à un attaquant de lancer du code sur un serveur web. Elle juge pourtant ce scénario « improbable » et ne publiera aucun correctif d’urgence.
Le 21 octobre, comme nous l’expliquions la veille, PHP avait corrigé en urgence deux failles bien plus graves, surnommées PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619). Elles permettent de prendre la main sur un serveur sans même avoir de compte. Les versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 et 8.2.35 les corrigent. Par contre, ces versions ne règlent pas la nouvelle faille, que PHP traite à part.
Une faille qui demande trois réglages bien précis
La nouvelle faille passe par les sessions, la mémoire qu’un site garde de votre visite, comme votre connexion ou votre panier. PHP enregistre ces données dans un format choisi par le réglage session.serialize_handler. D’après PHP, une application n’est exposée que si elle réunit trois conditions :

articles.title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016
articles.summary:
Prince of Persia, a threat group sponsored by the Iranian government, ran one of its command-and-control (C&C) servers from the United States this year, after a months-long lull in its operations, according to Semperis.
The APT actor, also tracked as Infy, has been operating for close to 20 years. Its targets are mostly Iranian dissidents, along with government and private entities in the US, Europe, and the Middle East.
Tomer Bar, AVP of security research at Semperis, tracked the group in his previous role at SafeBreach. He says that within a week of SafeBreach’s February 2026 report, the hackers took a C&C server offline and later relocated the rest of their servers.
Prince of Persia then halted operations for three months, a longer silence than any other in its nearly two-decade history. The pause overlapped with the war between Iran and the US and Israel, which broke out on February 28.
Semperis told SecurityWeek that this is the longest downtime it has confirmed, as its researchers were monitoring the group’s infrastructure the entire time. Earlier quiet periods reflected gaps in researchers’ visibility into the group’s operations rather than confirmed inactivity.
Prince of Persia’s operations restarted on May 27 with the deployment of a new C&C server, and data theft resumed. Within seven days, Tonnerre, one of the group’s malware families, had siphoned over 1,800 files from a single victim.

articles.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
articles.summary:
Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
A video player seeking to the middle of a movie asks for a few megabytes. Under our old range caching, that one request could make Cloudflare pull 128 MiB from the origin and move it between data centers, sometimes after the viewer had already left. Range requests are how large files get delivered, and caching them naively easily leads to wasted network bandwidth and wasted disk operations when running a CDN at scale.
So we rebuilt how our cache handles them. For R2, Cloudflare's object storage, p99 time to first byte dropped by about half, and a follow-up improvement cut tiered cache traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.
Today, we're making that new implementation available as Origin Range Requests, a self-service feature on all plans. There's no range size to tune and no need to contact support. Turn it on with a Cache Rule, and Cloudflare handles the rest.
A request for part of a file
An HTTP range request asks for part of a resource instead of the whole resource. The client sends a normal GET with a Range header:
GET /movie.mp4 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Range: bytes=1048576-2097151
If the server supports the request, it returns 206 Partial Content and identifies the returned bytes with Content-Range:
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Range: bytes 1048576-2097151/524288000
Content-Length: 1048576

articles.title: La inteligencia artificial reduce a la mitad el tiempo para escribir código, pero el 25% de eso es “basura de IA”
articles.summary:
Un nuevo informe de la Fundación Linux halló que la inteligencia artificial acelera la producción de código, pero compromete su calidad.
Según el estudio, la IA reduce en un 52% el tiempo necesario para escribir código, aunque una cuarta parte de las solicitudes de incorporación de cambios (pull requests) generadas con esta tecnología se consideran de calidad deficiente, un fenómeno que los desarrolladores denominan “basura de IA” o “AI slop”.
El trabajo analiza el impacto de las herramientas generativas en las comunidades de software de código abierto, donde los mantenedores de proyectos revisan y aprueban las contribuciones de los desarrolladores.
La proporción de código de baja calidad crece en los proyectos más grandes
La investigación determinó que el 25% de las solicitudes de incorporación de cambios recibidas se clasifica como de baja calidad. Esa cifra se eleva al 31% en el caso de los proyectos de código abierto de mayor tamaño, donde el volumen de contribuciones resulta más difícil de gestionar para los equipos de mantenimiento.
El 59% de los mantenedores señaló que experimentó un aumento en las contribuciones desde que las herramientas de IA generativa se popularizaron. Entre los proyectos grandes, ese porcentaje llega al 69%. articles.title: The first broken iPhone Duos are here
articles.summary:
The iPhone Duo officially goes on sale today, but a few units already have broken screens. According to posts on Reddit about the affected units, the issue appears to be happening at a similar spot on all of them: Some kind of problem shows up on the inner screen along the hinge and a strange bright line (or lines) across the right side of the display.
The first broken iPhone Duos are here
Now that the first folding iPhone has launched, we’ll find out quickly what can go wrong.
Here’s how one user in Australia described what happened to their phone:
Had my iPhone Duo for about six hours and had probably opened it fewer than 20 times.
I was showing it to a friend, and as I opened it, I felt something around the internal hinge, underneath the screen.
As I continued opening it, I heard an audible crack, and the screen broke right along the hinge.
There were no marks or damage on the inner screen’s surface or the external hinge to suggest anything had been caught or damaged.
The user said that the Apple Store replaced their phone with “a brand-new one on the spot.”
A post showing an image of another broken screen includes a video in a comment demonstrating yet another.
And a separate Reddit thread collected other pictures of affected Duos.

Atlassian’s vulnerability disclosure portal also lists CVE-2026-65905, a critical-severity Apache Tomcat flaw affecting Data Center and Crowd, among the issues disclosed on October 20. However, the CVE doesn’t appear in the bulletin, and the portal lists fewer unique CVEs than the bulletin does.
The remaining high-severity flaws affect widely used open source libraries, including Apache Tomcat, Netty, Bouncy Castle, Jackson, Axios, Spring, Apache Struts, and Apache ActiveMQ.

articles.title: Les banques sont « horrifiées » : des IA ont fait irruption dans des comptes bancaires

Interrogés sur la question, plusieurs responsables pointent du doigt une « situation effarante ». L’un des dirigeants précise que le secteur bancaire nourrit de « graves inquiétudes » à l’idée que des agents IA prennent des mesures « susceptibles d’affecter les finances des utilisateurs ».
À lire aussi : Deux ChatGPT ont pris des initiatives inquiétantes, et OpenAI ne comprend pas pourquoi
Une infraction aux règles bancaires
Comme le rapporte le média, l’intrusion commence lorsqu’un internaute confie ses identifiants à un assistant IA. Sans surprise, l’internaute veut déléguer certaines tâches à l’assistant. En se faisant passer pour le client, l’agent IA se connecte alors au compte, ce qui viole les règles de la plupart des banques. Les établissements bancaires exigent en effet que chaque personne se connecte elle-même à son propre compte.
Sur le papier, il n’est pas autorisé de déléguer l’accès à une IA. Dans certains des cas épinglés, les agents IA ne se sont pas contentés de consulter les transactions. Certaines IA ont contacté les centres d’appels de la banque et ont pris « des initiatives indépendamment des instructions de l’utilisateur ». En clair, des IA se sont mises à improviser diverses actions alors qu’elles avaient le contrôle du compte en banque

Uma fotografia composta registrou três meteoros da chuva Orionídeas cruzando um céu repleto de nebulosas e aglomerados estelares. A imagem foi capturada pelo astrofotógrafo Tim McCollum na madrugada de quarta-feira (21), enquanto a Terra atravessava a trilha de detritos deixada pelo cometa Halley.
O registro foi feito na cidade de Toccoa, no Estado da Geórgia (EUA). Embora o cometa esteja a mais de 4,8 bilhões de quilômetros da Terra, partículas liberadas por ele continuam produzindo rastros luminosos quando entram na atmosfera terrestre.
As Orionídeas parecem surgir de uma região próxima de Betelgeuse, estrela gigante vermelha da constelação de Órion. Na fotografia, os três meteoros aparecem cruzando o campo de visão em meio a objetos celestes distantes.
Como a imagem foi produzida
- Para registrar os meteoros, McCollum utilizou uma câmera Canon EOS Ra equipada com uma lente RF 28-70 mm f/2.0. O equipamento foi direcionado para a região aparente de origem dos meteoros com o auxílio de um rastreador de estrelas;

articles.title: Los envíos mundiales de computadoras cayeron 20% en el tercer trimestre por el encarecimiento de la memoria RAM

Los envíos mundiales de computadoras cayeron 20% en el tercer trimestre de 2026 frente al mismo período del año anterior, hasta 62,7 millones de unidades, según los datos preliminares que publicó IDC. Es la segunda caída trimestral consecutiva.
La consultora Omdia midió una baja similar, de 21%, hasta 58,1 millones de equipos, y Counterpoint Research ubicó la contracción en 21%. Las tres firmas coinciden en que se trata del derrumbe más pronunciado desde el primer trimestre de 2023.
El retroceso también rompió el patrón habitual del mercado: los envíos cayeron 9% respecto del segundo trimestre, cuando lo normal es que el tercer trimestre supere al segundo por la demanda de compras para la vuelta a clases.
“Lo que estamos viendo es el resultado de la fuerte anticipación de compras en el primer semestre. Los fabricantes y distribuidores acumularon inventario a comienzos de año para adelantarse a las subas de precios”, explicó Jitesh Ubrani, director de investigación de dispositivos de consumo en IDC.
Esa anticipación de compras dejó al tercer trimestre con poca demanda real para sostener el ritmo habitual de ventas. Según IDC, la causa de fondo son las restricciones de suministro y los precios más altos de los componentes, producto de la carrera de los centros de datos de inteligencia artificial por acaparar memoria.

Per LiteLLM’s investigation, the attackers obtained the GitHub CLI OAuth tokens for “an unexpected, innocuously named user account in our internal LiteLLM deployment, which was exposed to the public internet”.
The tokens were likely leaked by Claude Code, which, in specific circumstances, would embed them into a response body, which may be logged to LiteLLM logs. The attackers likely retrieved the tokens from the logs.
However, it is still unclear how the attackers accessed the internal deployment or moved laterally, as they had access to three sets of developer GitHub CLI credentials, LiteLLM says.
The attackers used the compromised credentials to disable branch protections, merge a change that pointed the releaser to a different source repository, and run a compromised GitHub workflow that pointed to a lookalike repository, then signed and published the poisoned artifacts.

articles.title: El miedo a la IA nace de nuestra incapacidad para entender cómo funciona. Un científico cree estar a punto de resolverlo

Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Leo Gao, Stephen Wolfram y Dario Amodei tienen al menos dos cosas en común. Todos ellos, junto a muchos otros científicos, han contribuido a que la inteligencia artificial (IA) alcance el grado de desarrollo que tiene actualmente. Y, además, todos han reconocido abiertamente que no comprenden por completo cómo los modelos de lenguaje organizan y utilizan internamente lo que han aprendido durante su entrenamiento. De alguna forma, se comportan como cajas negras cuyo contenido es relativamente inaccesible.
"Personalmente, no creo que lleguemos a interpretar nunca lo que sucede dentro de las redes neuronales por razones fundamentales, aunque podemos obtener algunas pistas interesantes. Mi esperanza reside más bien en conseguir que el proceso por el que la IA llega a sus respuestas pueda descomponerse en partes interpretables". Yoshua Bengio pronunció estas palabras durante una charla organizada por el Instituto para el Futuro de la Vida, en octubre de 2024. Geoffrey Hinton fue más breve en una entrevista con Wired de 2019: "No, realmente no sabemos cómo funcionan".

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:

- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Jusqu’ici, toutes les formules du Game Pass donnaient accès au cloud sans limite de temps. articles.title: The iPhone Duo should have been an iPad
articles.summary:
We gave the iPhone Duo a 7 /10. But that wasn’t always the score we planned, and it might not be the right score forever. Such are the challenges of reviewing — and assessing — a big, new idea about the most popular smartphone in history.
The iPhone Duo should have been an iPad
On The Vergecast: Notes on an iPhone Duo review, a PHP scandal, Brendan Carr, and more.
On this episode of The Vergecast, David and Nilay debate whether the Duo deserved the score it got, and try to work through how this device might change over time. Is the outer screen, as Daring Fireball’s John Gruber suggested, the worst iPhone ever? Would it be a better product if it started as an iPad rather than an iPhone? Would we feel differently about this thing if it were simply called the iPad Duo? It’s easy to see how the Duo will improve over time, but will it ever be the phone for everyone?
After that, the hosts talk about the huge PHP cybersecurity flaw that rocked the web this week and what it means for the future of the web, AI, and everything. It was a strange week for the web in general, as the ongoing increase in AI shopping has forced retailers everywhere to figure out how they want to interact with customers — and by customers, we mean Muse agents. Then it’s time for Brendan Carr Is a Dummy, an impending reboot inside of Netflix, and some very confusing Gemini news.

articles.title: Low-carbon concrete could lower emissions before data centres even go online |
articles.summary:
Concerns about the environmental impact of data centres have been popping across Canada almost as quickly as the data centres themselves. But what if there was a way to start lowering those emissions even before a facility is turned on? According to two cleantech advocates, greening the data centre boom starts with the buildings, and the huge amounts of concrete used to create them.
Concrete is responsible for roughly eight percent of the world’s carbon emissions, according to a study by Chatham House. Those emissions come primarily from the process of refining cement, the binding agent used in concrete. Traditional cement is created through a combustion process that both directly releases CO2 into the atmosphere and relies heavily on fossil fuels throughout manufacturing.
“If we’re looking at the concrete and steel that’s going to go into this project, we’re looking at somewhere between 218,000 and 263,000 tonnes of CO2.”
Gil Yaron, Light House
Data centres use a lot of concrete. According to Gil Yaron, the managing director of circular innovation at Light House, a Vancouver-based non-profit supporting regenerative building practices, Meta’s Sturgeon County data centre is predicted to require as much as 1.5 million cubic metres of concrete. That’s roughly the equivalent of 37 CN Towers.
Far from just an enormous physical footprint, that translates into a lot of emissions, according to Yaron.

Der Astrophysiker Mason Huberty von der University of Minnesota (USA) suchte nach bisher unentdeckten Objekten. articles.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Deploying a trained neural network involves more than translating each operator into a GPU kernel. It is a compilation problem with many legitimate answers. For example, when NVIDIA TensorRT builds an engine, it makes interdependent decisions about graph-IR transformations, fusion, implementation selection, memory placement, and quantization. This process is called scheduling. Different scheduling choices can preserve model semantics yet produce very different inference performance, making scheduling central to deep learning compiler optimization.
No single scheduling strategy is best for every model and deployment environment. A transformation that accelerates one network may slow another. A kernel that is faster in isolation may interact poorly with fusion, tensor layouts, or memory traffic elsewhere in the graph. Aggressive scheduling may improve performance while violating an application’s accuracy requirement. These coupled, model-dependent effects often appear only after the complete engine is built and measured, making the right strategy increasingly difficult to predict.
This post is Part 1 of a two-part series that is intended to develop a clearer way of reasoning about performance optimization. It explores questions such as: What makes one compiled engine better than another? Why can individually promising decisions fail end to end? How should accuracy constrain performance optimization? It introduces the Global Performance Tuner, a feature for automatic performance…

El directivo ubicó la capacidad de actualizar sistemas al mismo nivel que la detección de las fallas. articles.title: Quest Diagnostics Data Breach Exposed ‘Certain Patient Records’
articles.summary:
Medical laboratory operator Quest Diagnostics said it learned of a cyber breach of one of its systems this week, likely compromising some records for patients.
In a Thursday regulatory filing, Quest Diagnostics reported “unauthorized access” to its Quanum Lab Services Manager, a platform where certain clients can place test orders and receive or look up their results. The company said it discovered the hack on Wednesday and notified federal law enforcement.
How many patients and which particular records have been affected is still unknown. Quest Diagnostics said it believes “certain patient records” were accessed in the breach, but that the full scope remains under investigation.
The New Jersey-based company said it’s also working with external cybersecurity experts to assist in its response.
Quest Diagnostics has seen hacks impacting patient records before. In 2016, for example, the company said data including lab results and contact information of about 34,000 people was exposed in another online breach. And in 2019, other personal information belonging to about 11.9 million Quest patients was affected after a separate hack at American Medical Collection Agency, a billing collections service provider.
Cyberattacks are on the rise across industries. Beyond healthcare, other breaches have recently disrupted anything from supermarket chains to core education applications.

The original Apple iPod debuted 25 years ago today — Steve Jobs’ $399 device fit 1,000 songs into a package the size of a deck of cards with 5 gigabytes of storage
The chunky little original iPod packed a 1.8-inch Toshiba HDD, and used FireWire because the USB of the era was too slow and didn't offer charging.
On this day in 2001, Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPod. He began the presentation by teasing “a breakthrough digital device that’s not a Mac.” Ultimately, the iPod that was revealed that day became a pocket-sized digital music player phenomenon, and would be many gadget fans' favorite always-carry device before smartphones matured enough to make such things redundant. The key claim iPod launched with was that it could put your entire music library in your pocket for $399.
In October 2001, when the iPod launched, Steve Jobs had successfully steered Apple beyond the beige into the Mac OS X era, with iBooks and iMacs well established. A revival of the Cupertino company's fortunes was well underway, with these iDevices doing well among consumers – at a difficult time, not long after the dot-com bubble burst.
Jobs predicted that the “Mac could become the center of your digital lifestyle.” It would do so as a hub uniting digital cameras, digital camcorders, DVD players – and the portable music player. Apple decided to go down this avenue as everyone loves music and it’s a huge target market, without a market leader, reasoned the CEO.

AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) released security updates to patch 72 vulnerabilities in the Aruba Operating System (ArubaOS), including eight maximum-severity authentication bypass and code execution issues.
Also known as AOS, ArubaOS powers Aruba Networking enterprise wireless infrastructure, including mobility conductors, access points, controllers, and gateway devices.
The eight maximum-severity security flaws patched today affect multiple AOS-8 and AOS-10 software versions, and they can be exploited by remote threat actors without privileges through low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction.
HPE warned customers to patch these security issues as soon as possible and provided mitigation measures, including restricting access to AOS management interfaces.
"Customers are strongly urged to patch their instances due to the complexity, breadth, and impact of these vulnerabilities," the company warned in a Thursday security advisory.
"To minimize the likelihood of an attacker exploiting these vulnerabilities, HPE Networking recommends that the CLI and web-based management interfaces be restricted to a dedicated layer 2 segment/VLAN and/or controlled by firewall policies at layer 3 and above along with accounting controls for tracking and logging user activities and resource usage."

Uber le dio a la totalidad de sus 30.000 empleados acceso a ChatGPT Work, el agente de inteligencia artificial empresarial de OpenAI, luego de un plan piloto con 1.000 trabajadores. Es el primer despliegue de una plataforma de agentes de IA que abarca a toda la compañía, según anunciaron ambas empresas.
ChatGPT Work se conecta con herramientas que Uber usa a diario, como Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar y Slack. Según la descripción oficial de OpenAI, el agente puede investigar información, preparar resúmenes de reuniones, armar presentaciones, analizar datos y completar tareas que cruzan varias aplicaciones.
OpenAI presentó ChatGPT Work en julio como un agente capaz de tomar acciones dentro de las aplicaciones y archivos de un usuario y sostener una tarea durante horas. During the intrusion, the hackers stole the email addresses of 11,774,247 people, along with account data such as creation date, last login date, number of logins, and the last login’s IP address.
For 43 of the affected customers, the hackers also compromised dates of birth, gender information, country/region details, and nicknames.

Capcom says it implemented incident response measures and all services using CAPCOM ID remain available.
“In addition, we have started to contact the target customers sequentially, and we have established a dedicated contact point for customers regarding this matter,” an automated translation of Capcom’s incident notice reads.

articles.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 2 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
The Global Performance Tuner is a feature for automatic performance tuning released in NVIDIA TensorRT 11.1. It provides automatic, accuracy-aware and end-to-end performance tuning within TensorRT by customizing different optimizations for different models. For more details, see Part 1 of this series, which introduces the challenges associated with scheduling (a critical stage in deep learning compiler optimization), the motivation for developing the Global Performance Tuner feature in TensorRT, and the mathematical theories established to formalize the problem.
This post, Part 2, uses the notation from Part 1 to describe the algorithm and architectural design of the Global Performance Tuner feature. It also provides best practices for using it.
Designing the Global Performance Tuner feature in TensorRT
The central design idea of the Global Performance Tuner is to represent alternative scheduling strategies as explicit and searchable build routes. A compiler knob (also called a compiler flag or compiler option) is a configuration setting that changes some aspect of the compilation pipeline, such as a heuristic, fusion decision, or code generation path.
Each tunable knob exposes a finite set of allowed values and has a default value. A build route is a concrete combination of knob values. When no build route is specified, TensorRT uses the default build route, in which every knob retains its default value.

articles.title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?
articles.summary:
Headlines warn that AI could threaten humanity, and it’s easy to wave that off as science fiction. But the real danger is more ordinary and already here.
Research published by Gen Threat Labs demonstrated how quickly an AI agent’s autonomy can become a liability. In a controlled experiment, researchers manipulated an agent through content it encountered while reading email, prompting it to execute system commands, transmit data outside its environment and perform destructive file operations.
No software vulnerability was required. The agent simply treated untrusted content as instruction.
That autonomy is expanding daily. Agents are moving from answering questions to taking action doing everything from executing code, connecting to services, managing files and making decisions on a user’s behalf.
The shift from developer-focused tools like OpenClaw to widespread use of personal assistants like Muse, happened quickly. Delegating work across platforms is becoming commonplace and how people interact with AI.
The risks extend beyond manipulating agents. In October, Gen Threat Labs documented Warden Stealer, malware targeting configuration files and local data associated with AI assistants and coding tools, potentially exposing credentials, access tokens and conversation histories.

But the high-margin subsidised programmes that kick-started the industry are being phased out, and operators are facing a new reality of low-margin operations at scale. Combined with the demographic squeeze on the European workforce, the industry looks ripe for automation. Maybe even for robots.
The problem is well-known and systemic. Transmission networks are aging – some 40% of Europe’s distribution grids are over 40 years old – and cross-border capacity is set to double. Successful exploitation could impact the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of both VCO and the data it manages.
“On an affected system, any authenticated user can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local ‘superuser operator’ user. This includes access to functionality that is intended for internal use only and which is not intended to be remotely accessible,” the company says.

articles.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
articles.summary:
The PHP security team has shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability that affects systems with non-default configurations and has no patch.
PHP is an open-source web development language used by nearly 70% of all websites on the Internet. According to VirusTotal estimates, more than 5.1 million PHP hosts are exposed online, and roughly 3.8 million have at least one port open to attacks.
According to a Friday advisory, this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-115560) can only be exploited when targeting systems "with an unusual combination of configuration and application code."
"An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled," the PHP team explained.
"Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release."
Until a security patch is available, the PHP devs suggested setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0, adding that "If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed."
This mitigation should have already been applied on Wednesday, before patching two other critical RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked colle…

Les ingénieurs de l’ESA et de Thales Alenia Space ont lâché la maquette début octobre, à environ 3 kilomètres d’altitude au-dessus d’un champ de tir de l’armée italienne. Le petit parachute de freinage s’est ouvert normalement. La grande voile pilotable qui devait ensuite guider l’engin s’est en revanche détachée pendant son déploiement, et la maquette a terminé sa chute sans plus rien pour la ralentir. articles.summary:
Batterie de voiture électrique : 3 ans de conduite réelle révèlent la faiblesse cachée qui surgit passé 170 000 km
Sous le plancher d’une voiture électrique, des dizaines de cellules travaillent en équipe. Il suffit que quelques-unes s’essoufflent plus vite pour que toute la batterie arrive en fin de vie, alors que les autres ont encore de la réserve. En épluchant les données de 116 voitures et 17 bus, des chercheurs ont mesuré l’ampleur du phénomène : près de 18 % de durée de vie en moins, et un seuil kilométrique au-delà duquel tout s’accélère.
Une batterie de voiture électrique assemble des dizaines, voire des milliers de cellules, censées vieillir au même rythme. Sur la route, elles divergent. Des chercheurs de l'Institut de physique chimique de Dalian (Académie chinoise des sciences), de l'université Chalmers en Suède, de l'Institut de technologie de Pékin et de la filiale européenne de Zeekr, marque premium du groupe Geely, ont épluché plus de trois ans de données issues de 116 voitures et 17 bus circulant en Chine.
Leurs travaux, publiés le 25 août 2026 dans Nature Energy, chiffrent à l'échelle de flottes entières un défaut jusqu'ici étudié en laboratoire ou sur de petits échantillons.

À la recharge, la cellule de moindre capacité atteint la première sa tension maximale, et le système de gestion coupe le courant pour toutes les autres. En pleine accélération, celle dont la résistance interne a grimpé…

Avec un nouveau pack proposé en Chine, Firefly (une marque du constructeur Nio) repousse les limites en inaugurant une batterie de 60 kWh embarquée dans un véhicule de 4 mètres.
Déjà remarquée pour son volume de coffre arrière de 404 litres et son coffre avant (frunk) de 92 litres, assez grand pour accueillir deux valises cabine, la citadine chinoise surprend encore avec une autonomie de 560 km selon la norme chinoise, soit environ 450 km WLTP. Est-ce que cela change vraiment la donne ?
60 kWh au lieu de 42 kWh sans rien toucher : mais comment ?
La Firefly a réussi à faire rentrer une batterie de 60 kWh dans une voiture dont l’empattement mesure 2,615 mètres. Ce nouveau pack batterie conserve exactement le même format extérieur et le même poids sur la balance que la batterie initiale de 42,1 kWh. Le secret tient à la chimie des cellules.
Pour y parvenir, la marque troque la chimie LFP d’entrée de gamme (cellules Sunwoda) contre une chimie NMC ternaire (nickel-manganèse-cobalt) fournie par CATL. Le gain de densité énergétique est de 43 % à volume strictement égal.
L’autonomie grimpe à 560 km sur le cycle chinois CLTC. En équivalent WLTP européen, la citadine peut légitimement viser entre 440 et 455 km mixtes. Une autonomie record ? Pas vraiment, et c’est probablement là que le bât blesse.

A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.

articles.title: 'Daddy's girl': Millicent Okumu’s road back to agriculture
articles.summary:
Millicent Okumu doesn’t leave you wondering whether she believes what she is saying. She speaks with energy, with clarity about whom she is building for. Ask where the company is heading, and there is little hesitation; ask whether she will still be running it in ten years, and the answer is no.
By then, she expects Agriflex, the Kenyan agricultural business she co-founded, to be operating in at least five African countries, to be sustainably profitable, and to be led by somebody else. She might take an advisory role. For now, however, the company occupies even the hours she supposedly spends away from it. At family gatherings, unfinished tasks follow her into the room.
Her father, a civil servant and farmer, raised cattle and grew enough food to support relatives beyond his household. She was close to him, but less enthusiastic about the farm. She avoided agriculture at school and university, only to find herself back in it through a logistics job at iProcure in 2017.
Now she sells farm inputs, deploys spraying drones and listens to farmers explain why a clever piece of technology might be of little use to them. That last part has meant slowing down plans and turning away investors.
“We are in 2026,” she says. “We are no longer in 2006.”
She is impatient for progress, but increasingly particular about what counts as progress, and who benefits.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

articles.title: CON, PRN und NUL: Warum du Dateien in Windows 11 nicht so benennen darfst
articles.summary:
Windows 11: Diese Dateinamen sind verboten – und der Grund stammt aus dem Jahr 1981
Obwohl Windows 11 ein modernes Betriebssystem ist und Microsoft darauf bedacht ist, viele Neuerungen zu implementieren, gibt es darin noch Relikte fast vergessener Zeiten. Dazu zählt etwa ein Feature, das nur wegen eines Kultspiels in Windows eingefügt wurde. Daneben gibt es aber auch alte Regeln, die Windows-User:innen heute noch einen Strich durch die Rechnung, oder besser gesagt die Dateibenennung, machen können.
Warum Windows 11 manche Dateinamen verbietet
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, gibt es eine Reihe von Namen und Kürzeln, die nicht für Dateien in Windows 11 genutzt werden dürfen. Versuchen es User:innen doch, verweigert das Betriebssystem die Eingabe und drängt darauf, einen anderen Namen für die Datei oder den Ordner zu wählen. Insgesamt sind es sechs Namenskategorien, teilweise mit mehreren Vertretern ihrer Art.
So können Dateien unter Windows 11 weder „CON“, „PRN“, „AUX“, noch „NUL“ genannt werden. Auch bei „COM1“ bis zu „COM9“ sowie „LPT1 bis zu „LPT9“ sperrt sich das Betriebssystem. Wie Microsoft-Entwickler Raymond Chen in einem Blog-Post schon vor einigen Jahren erklärte, stammt diese Regelung noch aus alten DOS-Zeiten. articles.title: Compromised TLS Certificates - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Compromised TLS Certificates
The Indian CA eMudhra Limited has eight TLS certificates with laughably weak private keys:
The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2384, or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.
“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”
Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”
At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.
The whole certificate regime has long been a mess:
The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest…

After unauthorized access to the multi-tenant application, the group attempted sign-ins at more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, with stolen ConnectWise app credentials that authenticated as the apps with no interactive user sign-in. Some of the group’s attacks reached privileged access less than three hours after initial targeting.
Automated password guessing, or password spraying, also targeted 327 accounts across eight organizations with more than 151,000 failed logons and no successes. The use of ARTEX, “a system of LLM-driven agents that run an autonomous penetration test,” sped up scanning and reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse. The agents can work around the clock “with little needed human interaction,” at a pace that “leaves defenders with little time to detect and respond.” It’s uncertain how the ConnectWise credentials were stolen or how many tenants were actually compromised.

El economista jefe de Goldman Sachs, Joseph Briggs, estimó que la inteligencia artificial podría desplazar hasta al 9% de los trabajadores de Estados Unidos durante la próxima década, una cifra equivalente a uno de cada once empleados del país.
La proyección aparece en una nota publicada el 22 de octubre por Briggs, economista global del banco, y fue adelantada por la revista Fortune. El 9% equivale a 15 millones de trabajadores que perderían su puesto a lo largo de lo que Goldman llama la “transición de la IA”.
Pero el hallazgo central de la nota no es el número, sino el momento en que ocurrirá. Según Briggs, “la disrupción laboral vinculada a la automatización es limitada cuando la economía está sana, pero se acelera durante las desaceleraciones cíclicas”.
Es decir, mientras el empleo y el crecimiento se mantengan firmes, las empresas tendrán menos incentivos para reemplazar personal con IA. El verdadero recorte de puestos llegaría recién cuando se desate una recesión, sostiene el economista.
“Las disrupciones laborales vinculadas a la IA podrían amplificar el ciclo económico general”, escribió Briggs en la nota difundida el jueves.
Cómo pasó pronóstico del 6% al 9%
La cifra no salió de la nada. En agosto de 2025, Briggs y la economista Sarah Dong habían calculado que la IA podría desplazar entre el 6% y el 7% de la fuerza laboral estadounidense, dentro de un rango posible de entre el 3% y el 14%.

The more unusual figure is the yearly price of KES 899 (7), which works out to about KES 75 ($0.58) per month and sits well below the monthly price, even under the KES 119 ($0.92) introductory rate on offer for the first six months. The discount is so steep it looks like a mistake. Development of the MPAA’s least-favorite app of the 2010s has been abandoned for years, but the “Netflix of Piracy” software is still installed on millions of devices that are just waiting to join a bot army. Researchers at Eye Security found the updater for a Popcorn Time fork called “Time4Popcorn” still running on tons of Windows, macOS, and Android devices located around the world, phoning home to now-abandoned web domains over unencrypted HTTP and running an outdated, insecure version of Chrome.
Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
What old and vulnerable software might be running on your PC right now?
Eye Security’s Niels Teusink says the updater could have been used to install and run basically any kind of software with full privileges, easily enabling someone to create a botnet just by taking over one of the domains, using a man-in-the-middle attack to target specific devices, or perform surveillance by identifying the machines running the software.
Their solution was to register one of the domains and use it to send their own update that instructed the updater to disable itself. Despite ethical concerns about the fix, the researchers say their only alternative “was to do nothing,” pointing out, “The update process wasn’t doing anything functional anyway, it was only creating risk for users.”

Authentication does not equal authorization: Are we asking passkeys to prove too much?
A passkey confirms who logged in, not what they intended
By nearly all accounts, we’re inching closer to a passwordless society. The FIDO Alliance, which develops new passwordless authentication standards and whose tagline is quite literally “reducing reliance on passwords”, now estimates that more than 5 billion passkeys are in use worldwide. In fact, more than three-quarters of global consumers have already enabled a passkey on at least one account.
The technology is a boon for the financial industry because it finally removes the sector’s entrenched dependency on knowledge-based credentials – reusable “secrets” that criminals can steal, guess, or extract through social engineering. Suddenly, being able to quote a user’s mother’s maiden name, the town they grew up in, or their several-digit password, isn’t enough – and that makes user access instantly more secure.
Passkeys also give customers a much easier ride when it comes to accessing their accounts, speeding up the process by allowing them to use a key biometric like a fingerprint rather than hopping through two or three screens and entering their “memorable information” each time they log on.

articles.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide
Most fine-tuning teaches a model to produce a better answer to a single prompt. Agentic tasks are different. An agent that files an expense report or triages a support ticket takes a sequence of actions, and each step depends on what came before. There’s rarely one correct sequence to imitate, and the only reliable feedback is whether the whole sequence succeeded. Supervised fine-tuning has no labels for that, and single-turn reinforcement learning cannot credit a decision made three steps before the outcome.
Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI trains models on exactly that signal. SageMaker AI sends prompts to an agent you host on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, or on your own infrastructure, such as Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), or AWS Fargate, through an AWS Lambda forwarder. The example here uses AgentCore. The agent calls the policy model being trained, acts in your environment over as many turns as the task needs, and reports one reward when the episode ends. You don’t specify the right trajectory, only how to score the result.
This post uses Wordle, a game in which a player has six tries to guess a hidden five-letter word, as the example. After each guess, every letter turns green if it is in the right position, yellow if it’s in the word but in a different position, and gray if it isn’t in…

Factores como la luz, la temperatura, la calidad del aire y el ruido de fondo forman parte de un conjunto de condiciones que puede facilitar el trabajo intelectual o, por el contrario, sumar pequeñas distracciones que terminan afectando el rendimiento frente a la pantalla.
Un estudio publicado en 2025 en la revista Building and Environment, realizado con trabajadores de oficinas de cuatro países, encontró que una menor concentración de dióxido de carbono en el ambiente se asocia con mejores resultados en pruebas de pensamiento creativo divergente.
La misma investigación identificó que las temperaturas interiores de entre 22 y 26 grados Celsius están vinculadas a mejores puntuaciones de creatividad. Estos hallazgos no apuntan a la existencia de una oficina perfecta, sino a que el pensamiento creativo también responde a condiciones físicas concretas que pueden medirse y ajustarse.
Por qué el aire y la temperatura condicionan el pensamiento creativo
El aire que se respira durante la jornada frente a la computadora rara vez se tiene en cuenta como parte del espacio de trabajo. Sin embargo, el estudio de Building and Environment mostró una relación directa entre los niveles de CO2 y el desempeño en tareas de creatividad divergente.

NgRx, the reactive state management framework for Angular, has released version 22, shipping utilities for customising Angular's resource API, dynamic deep signals for union types, a new SignalStore typing helper and ESLint v10 compatibility.
The main new addition is resource extensions, delivered through a new experimental @ngrx/signals/resource entry point. Angular's resource and httpResource APIs reset value() to undefined while reloading and throw when read in an error state. Resource extensions wrap an existing resource and patch only those behaviours, while preserving the original resource type.
Four built-in extensions are included, alongside a provideResourceExtensions function that registers defaults at application, route or component level. In the original RFC, Marko Stanimirović explained that changing the error behaviour is also a prerequisite for deeper SignalStore integration, as "once a resource enters the error state, any subsequent patchState call will throw because it reads value() internally".

Windows Server 2016 was released in September 2016 at Microsoft's annual Ignite conference and reached general availability one month later, on October 12, 2016

“In Egyptian schools, English lives in the school book and stays there,” co-founder and CEO Mariam Soliman told Disrupt Africa. “I saw three problems up close. Practice stops at the classroom door: at home, nothing connects to the lesson a child just learned. The apps parents download are fun, but they teach their own course, not the one the child is tested on. And nobody – teacher, principal or parent – sees how a child is doing until the exam. In Upper Egypt, add weak internet and old devices, and most digital products simply don’t work.”
Founded in Assiut in Upper Egypt, Learning Rockets launched the first prototype of its Bee Degree app in 2023, with the idea for the business having started at home.
“My daughter became fluent in English because we taught it to her at home, and I kept asking myself – why can’t other children in Upper Egypt have the same chance?” Soliman said. “I had spent more than 10 years in business and finance, and I decided to build that chance myself.”

SecurityWeek’s weekly cybersecurity news roundup offers a concise overview of important developments that may not receive full standalone coverage yet remain relevant to the broader threat landscape.
This curated summary highlights key stories across vulnerability disclosures, emerging attack methods, policy updates, industry reports, and other noteworthy events to help readers stay well-informed about the evolving cybersecurity environment.
Here are this week’s highlights:
Heartbreaker macOS ransomware rebuilds itself from source
Researcher Patrick Wardle has analyzed Heartbreaker, a Rust-based macOS ransomware sample that was uploaded to VirusTotal in May 2025 and, as of his writing, was still undetected by every antivirus engine on the service. After attempting to set up a LaunchAgent for persistence, it encrypts files in the user’s Downloads folder. It then tries to change its hash by taking its own embedded source code, randomizing identifiers and adding junk functions, and recompiling itself (even trying to install Rust if it’s missing). Wardle believes it’s unlikely to be a major threat in its current form, as it uses a single hardcoded AES key that makes free file recovery possible, and its rebuild process depends on a Rust framework that’s no longer publicly available.

En España, es demasiado común reconocer el guion de la vivienda protegida: se construye sobre suelo público, se protege durante unas décadas y, cuando vence el plazo, el piso pasa al mercado libre, momento que aprovechan las sociedades y fondos de inversión para adquirir a precio base. En Donostia, el Gobierno vasco ha decidido cambiar ese final y apostar por el “modelo vienés”.
Su Departamento de Vivienda ha alcanzado un principio de acuerdo con Testa Residencial, sociedad vinculada a Blackstone, para adquirir por 100 millones de euros el derecho de superficie de 510 viviendas protegidas del barrio de Benta Berri. La firma está prevista para finales de este año y, cuando llegue, los pisos tendrán calificación de protección pública permanente.
La cifra: 196.000. Es lo que sale por vivienda al dividir los 100 millones entre 510. El Ministerio de Vivienda aporta unos 30 millones, y el Gobierno vasco paga el resto a plazos. El consejero Denis Itxaso sostiene que el coste es similar al de construir desde cero otras tantas viviendas, así que sale a cuenta. Los 1.700 residentes seguirán pagando alquileres de entre 600 y 1.000 euros al mes —Euskadi sigue en el top 5 en cuanto a precio de vivienda—. Además, quienes más vivienda poseen tienden a cobrar alquileres más caros que los dueños particulares.

OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
AI agents can still communicate without a network connection, OpenAI found.
OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September, after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies, or swarm obscure websites. El sistema fue desarrollado junto con investigadores de la Academia Zhongguancun, en China, el Instituto Telethon de Genética y Medicina y la Universidad Federico II de Nápoles, en Italia. Tiene 14.800 millones de parámetros y se entrenó con 302.000 millones de fragmentos de texto que combinan secuencias genéticas, literatura científica e instrucciones en inglés. El usuario pega una secuencia de ADN en una conversación de chat y el modelo responde con una explicación en texto.
Carbon-X puede predecir si una mutación genética es benigna o está asociada a una enfermedad, identificar qué regiones de una secuencia regulan la actividad de un gen, clasificar fragmentos de ADN según el organismo de origen y anticipar las bases siguientes de una secuencia.
Lewis Tunstall, científico investigador senior de Hugging Face, describió la herramienta como una forma de ampliar el acceso a este tipo de análisis. “Hemos desbloqueado una nueva capacidad en los modelos de lenguaje, que consiste en poder conversar con el ADN”, dijo. Each scanner report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the suspected vulnerability. Router vernetzen zahlreiche Haushalte mit dem Internet. Sie können aber schnell zum Einfallstor für Cyberkriminelle werden, wenn du nicht die richtigen Einstellungen am Router vornimmst. Gleiches gilt, wenn es eine Lücke im System der Router gibt, die lange Zeit unerkannt bleibt. So soll es laut einem Sicherheitsforscher schon seit 2010 der Fall sein. Die Fehler sorgen dafür, dass sich Unbefugte über WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) Zugriff auf die Router verschaffen können. Über das Feature können Endgeräte und Router ohne Passworteingabe miteinander verknüpft werden, indem eine WPS-Taste auf dem Router gedrückt wird, während das Endgerät ebenfalls einen WPS-Prozess startet. The rollout is part of a targeted release phase expected to end by mid-November, with the new security feature likely reaching general availability worldwide between early and mid-December.
Microsoft first revealed in a Microsoft 365 Roadmap entry last week that the AI-powered phishing detection will use conversation context (without retaining message content) to identify phishing and suspicious behavior in higher-risk messaging scenarios, such as external first-contact chats.

"The capability analyzes conversation context to identify suspicious behavior that may not include traditional indicators such as malicious links or files."
Microsoft says IT admins won't need to take any action to enable this new security protection feature, which will focus on external first-contact chats for most users.
It also added that while the new Teams feature will analyze conversation context to discover suspicious behavior, it will not retain customer data for further AI training or other uses.

Nigerian business banking platform Nomba has extended its Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) payments corridor into Zambia, allowing Congolese businesses to pay Zambian suppliers instantly.
Founded by Yinka Adewale and Pelumi Aboluwarin in 2016, and formerly known as Kudi, Nomba has evolved over the years into a profitable, omnichannel payment service provider.
Across its DRC operations and Canadian-licensed money service business, Nomba – which raised a US$30 million pre-Series B funding round in 2023 – processes more than US$480 million a month.
Disrupt Africa reported last month the startup had secured a US$ 3 million debt facility to scale that figure to US$1 billion monthly, starting with DRC, where businesses on its platform collect and pay in both US dollars and Congolese francs (CDF).
Working with licensed local partners, Nomba now enables these businesses to make payments in CDF and USD to suppliers in Zambia, with funds landing instantly in bank accounts or mobile wallets.

articles.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks
articles.summary:
Researchers remotely disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, a fork of the Popcorn Time BitTorrent client, closing a security flaw that could have allowed attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on millions of computers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-30612, affects Windows and macOS updaters that contacted the app's abandoned domain (popcorntimeupd.xyz) over unencrypted HTTP and accepted executables without verifying digital signatures.
Anyone controlling the update domain could manipulate HTTP traffic and execute code as SYSTEM on Windows and as root on macOS.
The Popcorn Time app featured a Netflix-style interface that integrated BitTorrent downloads, allowing users to consume illegal content right directly inside the app.
The project was abandoned for legal reasons but later relaunched as a legitimate content-streaming app. However, forks such as Time4Popcorn emerged under the Popcorn Time name, quickly attracting millions of users.
Researchers at Eye Security discovered the security risk after registering the popcorntimeupd.xyz domain and observed up to 3 million Windows and 350,000 macOS client connections to Time4Popcorn.
Connections came from residential ISPs and corporate, government, and military networks. However, none of the users appeared to be actively using the app, suggesting it had been installed and forgotten.

Attention le reste de l’article divulgâche la série Carrie.

articles.title: Oups, ce bug sur Signal permettait d'écouter la conversation même après avoir raccroché
articles.summary:
Une faille critique corrigée dans la bibliothèque d’appels de Signal permettait à un correspondant de continuer à capter votre audio après que vous aviez raccroché. Le correctif existe depuis début septembre, mais la vulnérabilité vient seulement d’être rendue publique.
La faille, référencée CVE-2026-113380, touche toutes les versions de RingRTC antérieures à 2.72.0. Elle affiche un score de 9,3 sur 10 sur l’échelle de sévérité CVSS.
Une faille corrigée qui donne quelques sueurs froides
RingRTC est la bibliothèque open source derrière les appels vocaux et vidéo de Signal, sur mobile comme sur ordinateur. La faille ne touche pas le chiffrement des conversations. Elle concerne uniquement la façon dont un appel se termine. Aucun message, mot de passe ou historique n’a été exposé, et changer ses identifiants ne sert à rien ici.
Pour fonctionner, RingRTC s’appuie sur des machines à états. C’est un composant logiciel qui suit chaque étape d’un appel, et chaque action passe par une file d’événements. Y compris quand on raccroche et termine l’appel. Un appelant malveillant peut saturer cette file avec des requêtes. La demande de fin d’appel envoyée par votre téléphone n’est alors jamais traitée. L’appel paraît terminé à l’écran, mais votre micro continue d’émettre vers votre correspondant. Il devient alors possible d’entendre une remarque lâchée après avoir terminé l’appel, une discussion avec quelqu’un à côté ou du simple bruit de fond. Le descriptif de la vulnérabilité évoque aussi…

articles.title: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Cloud providers in multi-cloud systems charge for data leaving their network, not entering it. The egress costs accumulate silently and are rarely caught before deployment.
- Architecture determines egress cost more than per-unit transfer rates. Where services are placed and how often they communicate matters far more than what you negotiate on billing rates.
- FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) provides a unified billing format across cloud providers, reducing normalization effort, but service-level attribution still requires provider-specific fields, ownership metadata, and network telemetry.
- Replacing continuous cross-cloud data transfer with scheduled synchronization reduces costs significantly without degrading service performance.
- Architecture had a larger impact on cost than provider pricing. In the controlled experiment, changing the communication pattern from synchronous cross-cloud processing to near-source processing saved over $2000 per month, while changing the provider rate saved $825 per month.
Introduction
Multi-cloud architectures give teams the flexibility to optimize for availability, vendor capabilities, and geographic reach. But this flexibility carries a hidden cost due to data movement across cloud provider boundaries. The costs accumulate through service placement decisions, communication patterns, and scaling behavior compounding over time. By the time it shows up on a bill, the architectural damage is done.

Pour y parvenir, il aurait fait appel au modèle V4.1 Flash 1017 de l’entreprise chinoise DeepSeek. Autant dire que les capacités de certaines IA chinoises ont de quoi inquiéter les États-Unis.

Finding the exact date of a masterpiece

- Study says the painting was made on July 22, 1889
- The researchers used AI and CAD tools to help find an answer
The Starry Night by Vincent Van Gogh is one of the most famous paintings in the world, and it’s generally held that the artist finished the work in June 1889, shortly before a serious mental breakdown. But a new scientific study has attempted to see if technology can find the exact date that the masterpiece was made — and it’s come to a quite different conclusion to past experts.
Research published in the journal Scientific Reports argues that not only was the painting based on a real night sky rather than pulled from Van Gogh’s imagination, but that July 22, 1889 is the most likely candidate for the date of the composition. However, while the model is indeed cheap and scores well, it can be hallucination-prone.

articles.title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs. Announced on October 9, 2026, the feature generates interactive flamegraphs through the Workers Observability dashboard or the cf CLI, helping teams identify expensive functions and memory allocations without relying solely on logs and aggregate metrics.
Developers can capture CPU or heap-allocation profiles for a deployed Worker version and inspect the results as a flamegraph, where wider sections indicate functions responsible for a larger share of CPU time or sampled memory allocations. Profiles can also be downloaded for offline analysis.
The key distinction is that profiling targets an already-running isolate rather than starting a fresh one. This allows developers to examine code executing under real production traffic. Durable Objects receive additional support for profiling a specific named instance, which is useful when investigating problems tied to stateful workloads. However, the target must receive sufficient traffic during the capture window, and TypeScript developers should enable source maps to make function names easier to interpret.

Schools may be located far away, and a lack of essential documents can make it difficult to access government services. Limited awareness of welfare schemes adds to the challenges. If you own a Pebble smartwatch (or are thinking of getting one), a major update is on the way: plug-in support is coming to the Pebble OS platform, which will mean much more flexibility and variety for apps and watch faces.

Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants.
Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round. Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform.

Pesquisador identificou falha que permite rodar aplicativos não oficiais e modificar jogos no console.
O Nintendo Switch 2 foi desbloqueado pela primeira vez via software, pouco mais de um ano após o lançamento. Batizado de ns2jb, o método permite executar código não autorizado sem instalar modchips ou realizar modificações físicas no console.
A descoberta foi apresentada pelo pesquisador Sammy Hajhamid, conhecido como “pepsipu”, e funciona na versão 23.0.1 do sistema, atualmente o firmware mais recente do Switch 2. O jailbreak, no entanto, possui limitações e não oferece o mesmo nível de acesso que usuários conseguiram ao desbloquear o Switch original.
O processo é feito apenas por software e não exige abrir o videogame ou soldar componentes na placa. Segundo o pesquisador, o ns2jb aproveita falhas encontradas no SmileBASIC 4, aplicativo de programação criado para o primeiro Switch e executado no Switch 2 graças à retrocompatibilidade.

articles.title: AWS Introduces Lambda Web Functions for Node.js Applications
articles.summary:
AWS recently introduced Lambda Web Functions, allowing developers to run Node.js web applications using frameworks such as Express and Hono directly on Lambda, with support for concurrent requests and response streaming.
According to the Lambda Web Functions documentation, the new functions support concurrent HTTP requests and response streaming. They charge for active CPU time and memory, rather than CPU time spent waiting for downstream services. Multi-Region routing directs requests to the closest Region, while a single warm execution environment can handle multiple concurrent requests, significantly reducing cold starts. Existing Lambda functions are now called Lambda Event Functions, with no changes required. Micah Walter, senior solutions architect at AWS, summarizes the benefits and why it removes this complexity:
You can take a standard port-listening server built with Express, Hono, Fastify, Next.js, or any Node.js framework, deploy it with a single command, and Lambda automatically handles scaling, multi-region distribution, and active CPU billing. No adapters, no infrastructure to manage, and no framework lock-in.
Endpoints use a Lambda-provided domain by default. To use a custom domain, edge caching, or AWS WAF, developers can use Amazon CloudFront in front, relying on Lambda Web Functions as the origin.

articles.title: Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai

Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai
At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman of EY GDS made the case that moving agents into production is an engineering problem, not a model problem.
Ask a room of developers about agents today and you will get plenty of answers. Almost everyone has built one, and most have a demo they are proud of.
The harder question is what happens after that, when the agent has to hold up against real customers, real data, and real consequences. At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman, Global Cloud Consulting, Microsoft Practice and Alliances Leader at EY GDS, opened with a version of it. He asked how many people in the room had built an AI agent, and plenty of hands went up. Then he asked how many had built one that made it to production for a business-critical system. "I think that's where the numbers dramatically drop," he said. "Not because of anybody's fault, but that's how it is."
That gap is the whole problem, and it is not a model problem. Cloud, low code tools, and open model APIs have pushed the entry barrier close to zero. What has not changed is the difficulty of industrializing what you build. "Access to intelligence is not the bottleneck, but the ability to industrialize is going to be the bottleneck," said Arvind Purushothaman.

articles.title: La desaparición del "sueño bifásico": cómo la Revolución Industrial eliminó la costumbre de dormir en dos tandas
articles.summary:
Despertarse en medio de la noche es algo habitual para muchos. Hoy en día es algo que vinculamos a problemas para dormir, pero para algunos, podría ser tan solo una reminiscencia de un hábito pasado arraigado en nuestros patrones de sueño desde hace siglos.
El sueño bifásico es un patrón de sueño en el que las horas de sueño se reparten en dos bloques separados por un periodo de vigilia. Se trata de un patrón de sueño popularizado por el historiador Roger Ekirch y por el psiquiatra Thomas Wehr que de manera independiente estudiaron el fenómeno.
Ekirch descubrió indagando en documentos que cubrían no sólo la edad media sino también la edad moderna una referencia recurrente a los “primeros sueños”. Esto lo llevó a compilar una serie de pruebas historiográficas, procedentes tanto de la ficción como de documentos oficiales, de la existencia de un sueño bifásico en estos periodos.

articles.title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
articles.summary:
CSIRO has developed Serverless Beacon (sBeacon), a serverless architecture for querying genomic variant data without copying large genomic datasets into a central database. The system uses Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon Athena, and Amazon DynamoDB to provide an implementation of the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH) Beacon standard, supporting genomic queries across large cohorts while keeping the underlying data in its original storage.
The architecture separates genomic data from the metadata needed to search it. Variant Call Format (VCF) files remain in Amazon S3, while metadata such as disease status, age, and location is indexed separately. During onboarding, sBeacon creates indexes and Athena tables for the metadata, while ontology terms are handled through CSIRO's Ontoserver to support queries combining genomic and phenotypic information.
sBeacon data onboarding architecture (Source: AWS Blog Post)
For variant queries, API Gateway routes requests to Lambda functions that identify relevant datasets and genomic regions. The Variant Querying Module uses bcftools and its htslib library to retrieve specific portions of VCF files through HTTP byte range requests. This allows the system to read the required genomic region without transferring the complete file. Results are aggregated and returned through the Beacon API.

articles.title: Two Dollars and a Test Suite - EE Times
articles.summary:
The Arm-Qualcomm verdict made headlines for its $2 award. The finding that matters more is about who controls the compliance tests a custom chip must pass before it can ship.
The verdict nobody read closely
On Oct. 13, a federal jury in Delaware delivered the second verdict in two years between Arm and Qualcomm. The number that drew the most attention was the damages award: $2, one for each claim Qualcomm won. Both companies declared victory, and IMHO both had some reason to. Arm prevailed on four of the six claims. On the other hand, Qualcomm won a finding that Arm interfered with its business with Meta, plus an additional finding under its Architecture License Agreement that I think deserves far more attention than it received.
The jury found that Arm breached Qualcomm’s Architecture License Agreement by withholding two deliverables, ACKs and OOBs. To most people, these acronyms mean very little, which may explain why most coverage moved quickly on to royalties and to the $2. But they describe something we may know very well: the tests a custom processor must pass before anyone can call it an Arm processor.
What a compliance kit actually does
Arm licenses its technology in two ways. Most customers take Arm-designed cores “as is” and integrate them into their chips, under a Technology License Agreement (TLA). articles.title: China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing
articles.summary:
China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing — DUV multiple patterning means bigger dies, lower yields, and longer manufacturing times
China has shown that older DUV lithography can be stretched much further than many expected – but can it fully catch up?
Export controls have kept ASML's most advanced EUV lithography machines out of China. Instead, the country's chipmaking industry has relied on less-capable deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines. By using multiple exposures on critical chip layers, these older machines are still capable of producing performant silicon. However, as multiple patterns are applied there are more chances for defects, longer manufacturing times, and higher bills. We spoke to experts like Chris Mack, co-founder and CTO of semiconductor firm Fractilia, to find out how much further DUV can go.
For years, extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography has been seen as China’s biggest choke point in the country’s attempts to build cutting-edge chips. The machines, made exclusively by Dutch manufacturer ASML, use 13.5nm-wavelength light to print some of the most intricate features found on modern processors. Sales of ASML’s EUV systems are subject to export restrictions, forcing Chinese manufacturers to squeeze ever more out of older deep ultraviolet, or DUV, lithography instead. The EUV gap alone between China and the West is at least half a decade, according to some analysts.
